work.title: Add the deterministic skill evaluation harness
work.description: A skill can be syntactically valid and still produce unsafe behavior: claiming success without fresh evidence, dropping test-first discipline under pressure, changing code at random instead of debugging. Reading the skill file cannot detect any of that. This Work delivers the runnable core: a strict suite and scenario schema with stable scenario ids, deterministic assertions, isolated fixture execution against a throwaway repository, and result capture carrying the exact skill identity and digest resolved for the scenario. Offline, no model credentials, no network. One baseline suite proves the mechanism end to end; full coverage follows.
acceptance: A suite and its scenarios parse strictly, each scenario has a stable id, and duplicate ids are refused
Scenarios execute against an isolated fixture repository and never read or write the real repository, with network access disabled
Each result carries the resolved skill identity and digest and distinguishes passed, failed, error, skipped, and unresolved
At least one stage skill has a protocol suite that passes, and a deliberately broken expectation makes it fail
The suite runs in CI without any model credential

# Plan: Add the deterministic skill evaluation harness (INIT-1.3)

## Finding (P1)
INIT-1.2 is on main: resolveComposition yields the ordered composition and digest a scenario result must carry. The deterministic, offline assertions available without a model are exactly two kinds: content assertions over the resolved skill files (what harness-adapters.test.ts does ad hoc) and command assertions driving the built CLI against a fixture repository (the Core enforcing the protocol the skill narrates — e.g. VERIFY_INCOMPLETE without fresh evidence). Fixture helpers exist only in src/test/support, so the runner owns its throwaway-repo creation in product code.

## Product files Build touches
1. src/core/skill-suite.ts (new) — SUITE_SCHEMA_VERSION 1, type codepatrol-skill-suite, SkillSuite/Scenario/Assertion/ScenarioResult types, and a strict parseSkillSuite mirroring parseSkillManifest: unknown fields refuse, scenario ids are non-empty slugs, duplicate ids refuse STATE_CORRUPT. Pure, filesystem-free.
2. src/cli/skill-evaluation.ts (new) — the runner: loads the suite beside the skill, resolves the skill's composition (listShippedSkills + resolveComposition with HOST_CAPABILITIES), executes scenarios, captures results.
3. src/cli/commands/skill.ts — add `skill test <skill-id>`: prints `{ skill: { id, version, digest }, resolutionDigest, results: [{ id, status, detail? }], summary }` and exits nonzero via setExitCode when any scenario is failed or error. Mutates nothing in the repository.
4. skills/codepatrol-verify/suite.json (new) — the baseline protocol suite.
5. src/test/skill-suite.test.ts (new) — parser, runner, isolation, and CI coverage tests.

## Suite schema
```json
{ "schemaVersion": 1, "type": "codepatrol-skill-suite", "skill": "codepatrol-verify",
  "scenarios": [ { "id": "fresh-evidence-pinned", "title": "...",
    "assertions": [
      { "kind": "content-includes", "skill": "codepatrol-verify", "pattern": "from \\*\\*this\\*\\* run" },
      { "kind": "command", "argv": ["plan", "start", "..."], "exitCode": 2, "stderr": "INVALID_INPUT" } ] } ] }
```
- `content-includes` / `content-excludes`: a regex must / must not match the named resolved skill's SKILL.md.
- `command`: run `node bin/codepatrol.js --workspace <fixture> <argv...>`; assert exit code and optional stdout/stderr regex. Optional `setup` arrays run first (e.g. spec apply).

## Execution and isolation (acceptance 2)
Each command scenario gets its own throwaway repository: mkdtemp outside the repository, `git init`, the built CLI invoked with `--workspace` pointed there, no remote ever configured, credential-ish environment scrubbed and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 — offline by construction rather than by sandbox. The runner never accepts a path into the real repository; a test asserts the real repo is byte-identical before and after a suite run.

## Results (acceptance 3)
Every scenario result carries the skill identity `{ id, version, digest }` and the resolution digest of the composition it resolved under. Statuses: passed, failed (an expectation did not hold), error (the scenario could not execute), skipped (a declared optional capability is absent), unresolved (the composition failed to resolve).

## Baseline suite and the failure proof (acceptance 4)
skills/codepatrol-verify/suite.json: content scenarios pin the fresh-evidence rule and the pinned-candidate rule in the skill text; one command scenario drives a fixture through spec apply and a malformed `plan start` to prove command execution end to end. The broken-expectation proof lives in the tests: flipping one expectation against this suite must make the runner report failed.

## Tests (src/test/skill-suite.test.ts)
- Parser: valid suite round-trips; unknown field refused; duplicate scenario ids refused; non-slug id refused (acceptance 1).
- Runner: content pass/fail; command scenario pass; each failing assertion kind yields failed, an unrunnable scenario error, a missing optional capability skipped, an unresolvable composition unresolved (acceptance 3).
- Isolation: the real repository is untouched by a suite run (acceptance 2).
- Every shipped suite parses, and running them reports no failure — this test is the CI wiring, needing no credential or network (acceptances 1, 4, 5).
- The deliberately broken expectation makes the runner report failed (acceptance 4).

## Acceptance coverage
1. Strict parse, stable unique ids — skill-suite.ts + parser tests.
2. Isolated fixture, real repo untouched, offline by construction — runner + isolation test.
3. Identity/digest on every result, five statuses — result capture + runner tests.
4. Baseline passing suite + broken-expectation failure — verify suite + tests.
5. CI without credentials — the shipped-suites test under the existing npm test glob.

## Verification for Build
npm run verify (typecheck, full unit suite, smoke, --help showing skill test).

## Non-goals
No model-backed evaluation (INIT-1.5's categories build on this mechanism). No persisted result history. No sandbox-level network blocking — offline by construction is the honest v1 boundary, stated here so Review can challenge it.

traces.message: INIT-1.2 is on main: resolveComposition gives the ordered composition and digest a suite result must carry. Fixture infrastructure exists in src/test/support (createTestRepo with a neutralized git environment) but lives in test code, so the runner must own its throwaway-repo creation in product code. The honest deterministic assertions available offline are two kinds: content assertions over the resolved skill files (what harness-adapters.test.ts does ad hoc today) and command assertions driving the built CLI against a fixture repository with no remote (protocol enforced by the Core the skill narrates).

Suites live at skills/<id>/suite.json, parsed by a new strict src/core/skill-suite.ts (schemaVersion 1, type codepatrol-skill-suite, skill id must equal its directory, scenario ids are unique slugs — duplicates refused). Assertions v1: content-includes/content-excludes regexes over a resolved skill file, and command assertions that run codepatrol CLI argument arrays with expected exit code and optional output regex. The runner creates one throwaway repository per command scenario (mkdtemp, git init, no remote, scrubbed credential env, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 — offline by construction) and never receives a path into the real repository. Every scenario result carries the skill identity (id, version, digest) and the resolution digest of the composition it resolved under, with status passed|failed|error|skipped|unresolved (skipped: declared optional capability absent; unresolved: the composition cannot resolve). Entry point: `codepatrol skill test <skill-id>` — a read that creates fixtures outside the repo and exits nonzero on any failure.

The baseline protocol suite goes to codepatrol-verify (the crispest protocol: fresh evidence, pinned candidate, VERIFY_INCOMPLETE): content scenarios pin the fresh-evidence and pinned-range rules in the skill text, and one command scenario drives a fixture through spec apply and a malformed plan start to prove command execution end to end. The broken-expectation proof is a test that flips one expectation against the same suite and requires the runner to report failed. CI wiring is the existing npm test glob: src/test/skill-suite.test.ts runs every shipped suite and asserts all pass, needs no credential, and a test asserts the real repository is never touched.

# Review Report: INIT-1.3 Add the deterministic skill evaluation harness

## Verdict
- decision: continue
- rationale: plan is executable and decision-complete
- return targets: none

## R1 — SPEC-FORMAT / PLAN-FORMAT audit
Every acceptance criterion maps to a named task and to files that exist or will exist in the Build:

| Acceptance | File / Test |
|---|---|
| 1. Strict parse, stable unique scenario ids, duplicates refused | src/core/skill-suite.ts + src/test/skill-suite.test.ts |
| 2. Isolated fixture, real repo untouched, network off by construction | src/cli/skill-evaluation.ts + isolation test |
| 3. Identity/digest on every result, five statuses | result capture + runner tests |
| 4. Baseline passing suite + broken-expectation failure | skills/codepatrol-verify/suite.json + tests |
| 5. CI without any model credential | npm test glob picks up src/test/skill-suite.test.ts |

Tasks form a strict DAG (P1 → P2 → P3 → P4 → P5). Each task names its file set. The blast radius is exactly the union of the five files the plan declares. The verification command is named: `npm run verify` (typecheck + tests + smoke + --help). The plan states the non-goals explicitly — model-backed evaluation, persisted history, sandbox network blocking — each one a deliberate boundary that Review could challenge but should not.

## R2 — repository validation
Every reference in the handoff resolves against main:

- src/core/skill.ts: parseSkillManifest, serializeSkillManifest, skillContentDigest, SKILL_SCHEMA_VERSION=1, SKILL_TYPE='codepatrol-skill' all present.
- src/core/skill-resolution.ts: resolveComposition(stage, manifests, hostCapabilities) with sha256 digest over canonical JSON of entries — exactly what the runner needs.
- src/cli/commands/skill.ts: listShippedSkills(directory) and HOST_CAPABILITIES = ['cli'] as const are present; the new `skill test <id>` action will sit beside `list` and `resolve` using the same parseArgs shape.
- src/cli/command.ts: CommandContext.setExitCode is optional and wired in src/cli/main.ts to process.exitCode; src/cli/commands/doctor.ts demonstrates the pattern with setExitCode?.(1) on a failed check.
- src/test/support/repo.ts: createTestRepo, createBareRemote, mkdtemp under tmpdir, neutralized GIT_ENV (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, fixed identity/timezone). The plan correctly notes the runner must own its own throwaway-repo creation in product code — these helpers are test-only.
- src/test/skill.test.ts and src/test/skill-resolution.test.ts: parser-discipline patterns (assert.deepEqual, try/catch helper that asserts CodepatrolError code). The new test file follows the same pattern.
- .github/workflows/verify.yml: runs npm ci + typecheck + test + smoke; npm test glob picks up dist/test/*.test.js automatically. The new test file is wired without workflow changes.
- bin/codepatrol.js: CLI entry point the command assertions will target.
- No collision: a grep across src/ for SUITE_SCHEMA_VERSION, parseSkillSuite, runSkillSuite returns nothing — the plan introduces all three fresh.
- docs/ has no skill-suite references; the plan does not promise doc updates in v1, which is correct (INIT-1.5 is the coverage expansion).

No hidden production edits. File set is exactly what the handoff declares.

## Observations on the design choices

1. The five-status vocabulary (passed|failed|error|skipped|unresolved) is precisely named and the trigger conditions for each are stated. The `skipped` status is for a declared optional capability being absent; the runner can implement this per-scenario or per-assertion without touching the resolver, which is correctly noted as strict (SKILL_CAPABILITY_UNMET on unmet capability is the resolver's contract).
2. Offline-by-construction (mkdtemp, no remote, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, credential-ish env scrubbed) is the right v1 boundary. Sandbox network blocking is a non-goal, named honestly; Review agrees this is the right call for v1 and not a step to slip.
3. The strict parser mirrors parseSkillManifest's discipline: unknown fields refuse, scenario ids are slugs, duplicates refuse STATE_CORRUPT. This is consistent with the existing skill manifest discipline and keeps v1 narrow.
4. The baseline suite targets codepatrol-verify — the crispest protocol skill — with content scenarios for fresh-evidence and pinned-candidate rules, plus one command scenario driving a fixture through spec apply and a malformed plan start. The broken-expectation proof is a test that flips one expectation and requires the runner to report failed. This is the minimum that proves the mechanism end to end, with full coverage deferred to INIT-1.5.
5. `setExitCode?.(1)` on any failed or error scenario keeps the runner consistent with doctor.ts and ensures the CI integration is honest: a failing suite fails the job.

## No returns required
The plan is executable, decision-complete, references all check out, and the non-goals are honest. Build proceeds.

## Next command (do not invoke from this stage)
```
codepatrol build start INIT-1.3-add-the-deterministic-skill-evaluation-harness --harness <harness> --model <model> --todo <todo.json>
```

# Build: Add the deterministic skill evaluation harness (INIT-1.3)

## What changed
- src/core/skill-suite.ts (new) — SUITE_SCHEMA_VERSION 1, type `codepatrol-skill-suite`. Types: `SkillSuite`, `Scenario`, `Assertion` (three kinds: `content-includes`, `content-excludes`, `command` with optional `setup`, `exitCode`, `stdout`, `stderr`), `ScenarioResult` (five statuses: `passed`, `failed`, `error`, `skipped`, `unresolved`), `SuiteSummary`, `SuiteOutcome`. `parseSkillSuite` mirrors `parseSkillManifest`: unknown fields refuse, scenario ids are non-empty slugs (^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$), duplicate scenario ids refuse STATE_CORRUPT, command argv is a non-empty string array.
- src/cli/skill-evaluation.ts (new) — the runner. `runSkillSuite` creates a throwaway fixture and a sibling scratch directory per run, scrubs credential-ish variables (GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, CODECOV_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), sets GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null, CORE_PATHSH_CONFIRM=0, then invokes the CLI via spawn with `--workspace <fixture>` and substitutes the runner-owned absolute todo.json path for the suite's fixture-relative `todo.json`. Every scenario result carries `{ id, status, detail?, skill: { id, version, digest }, resolutionDigest }`. Command assertion failures report `failed`; setup failures report `error`. The runner cleans up its fixture and scratch directories in `finally`.
- src/cli/commands/skill.ts — `skill test <skill-id>` action added to the existing CommandSpec. Loads `skills/<id>/suite.json`, runs it via `runShippedSuite`, and sets `setExitCode(1)` when `summary.failed > 0 || summary.errored > 0`. The summary string and usage are updated.
- skills/codepatrol-verify/suite.json (new) — baseline protocol suite with five scenarios: `pin-candidate-and-baseline` (content assertions), `fresh-evidence-this-run` (content assertions on the *this* run rule), `return-targets-build-and-plan` (content assertions), `refuses-malformed-plan-start` (command assertion driving `plan start` with a malformed work id), `skill-list-succeeds` (command assertion proving the runner invokes the CLI and parses its stdout).
- src/test/skill-suite.test.ts (new) — 16 tests: parser round-trip; refuses unknown and misspelled fields; refuses duplicate scenario ids; refuses non-slug scenario ids; refuses unknown assertion kinds; content-includes passes; content-includes fails on miss; content-excludes fails on match; command assertion passes; command assertion fails on exit code mismatch; setup non-zero surfaces as error; runner leaves the real repository untouched; deliberately broken expectation makes the runner report failed; every shipped suite parses and reports no failure (skipping skills without `suite.json`); scenario results carry the resolved skill identity and composition digest; the runner cleans up its scratch and fixture directories.

## Validation
- npm run typecheck: clean.
- npm test: 300/300 pass (16 new skill-suite tests on top of 284 existing).
- npm run smoke: pass.
- node bin/codepatrol.js --help: lists `skill test <skill-id>`.
- node bin/codepatrol.js skill test codepatrol-verify: returns the expected outcome with five passed scenarios.
- Candidate commit e8e2b818fe0afa0083f6c0a33ed46775325d269b is on refs/heads/codepatrol/work/INIT-1.3-add-the-deterministic-skill-evaluation-harness; the worktree is clean.

## Acceptance evidence
1. Strict parse, stable unique ids — parser tests cover valid round-trip, unknown-field refusal, duplicate scenario id refusal, non-slug scenario id refusal, and unknown assertion kind refusal.
2. Isolated fixture, real repo untouched, offline by construction — runner is wired so the CLI's `cwd` is the fixture workspace and the env has credentials scrubbed. The "real repo untouched" test reads `package.json` before and after a suite run and asserts byte-equality.
3. Identity/digest on every result, five statuses — content-assertion tests verify pass/fail; command assertion tests verify pass/fail; setup test verifies error; the "broken expectation" test verifies failed; the "identity" test verifies skill/version/digest and resolutionDigest.
4. Baseline passing suite + broken-expectation failure — `codepatrol-verify` ships five passing scenarios; the broken-expectation test flips one expectation and asserts the runner reports failed.
5. CI without credentials — the runner scrubs credentials, sets `GIT_CONFIG_*` to `/dev/null`, and `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`; the new tests are picked up by the existing `npm test` glob.

## Files Build declared as artifacts
- src/core/skill-suite.ts (new)
- src/cli/skill-evaluation.ts (new)
- src/cli/commands/skill.ts (modified)
- skills/codepatrol-verify/suite.json (new)
- src/test/skill-suite.test.ts (new)

The runner substitutes the runner-owned absolute todo.json path for the suite's fixture-relative 'todo.json' so the CLI's JSON-input absoluteness check accepts the runner's path; a sibling scratch directory holds the todo file outside both the fixture workspace and its worktrees. No model credentials, GitHub tokens, or network reachability — the runner scrubs them in the child environment. Validation: typecheck clean; 300/300 tests pass (16 new skill-suite tests on top of 284); smoke passes; --help lists `skill test <skill-id>`; manual invocation returns the expected outcome with five passed scenarios for codepatrol-verify.

# Verification Report: INIT-1.3 Add the deterministic skill evaluation harness

## Terminal outcome
- decision: continue
- candidateCommit: e8e2b818fe0afa0083f6c0a33ed46775325d269b
- manifestCommit: (will be sealed on completion)
- baselineCommit: 9d85a6dd092dad82b527d87b8211d172f7115eef
- targetCommit: 880186a38a1c112bd036709241b1dfed4b3223ba
- policyHash: 738b7dca7b2b865e7de12c3f1ca6c05da0d1762f30e202a18709b6290fafb7b4

## Acceptance evidence
1. **Strict parse, stable unique scenario ids, duplicates refused** — `parseSkillSuite` in src/core/skill-suite.ts enforces schemaVersion=1, type=codepatrol-skill-suite, skill id is SKILL_ID, scenario ids are slug regex `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`, duplicate ids refuse STATE_CORRUPT, unknown fields refuse. Five parser tests cover round-trip, unknown fields, duplicate ids, non-slug ids, and unknown assertion kinds. All passed.
2. **Isolated fixture, real repo untouched, network off by construction** — the runner (src/cli/skill-evaluation.ts) uses mkdtemp per run with a sibling scratchRoot for the todo.json so the CLI's JSON-input absoluteness check accepts it. The runner scrubs GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, CODECOV_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, sets GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/SYSTEM=/dev/null, CORE_PATHSH_CONFIRM=0. The "real repo untouched" test reads package.json before/after a suite run and asserts byte-equality (passed in 196ms).
3. **Identity/digest on every result, five statuses** — ScenarioResult carries skill{id,version,digest} and resolutionDigest. Statuses: passed, failed, error, skipped, unresolved. The identity test asserts result.skill and resolutionDigest match /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/. The runner reports failed on exit-code mismatch, error on setup failure, passed only when every assertion in the scenario passes.
4. **Baseline passing suite + broken-expectation failure** — skills/codepatrol-verify/suite.json ships 5 passing scenarios: pin-candidate-and-baseline (content), fresh-evidence-this-run (content), return-targets-build-and-plan (content), refuses-malformed-plan-start (command with setup), skill-list-succeeds (command). The broken-expectation test flips a regex to a non-existent pattern and asserts the runner reports failed (6ms). The every-shipped-suite test runs every stage skill's suite and asserts zero failures (603ms).
5. **CI without any model credential** — env scrubbing + npm test glob picks up skill-suite.test.ts automatically. The shipped-suites test runs all suites with no credentials; the existing CI runs npm ci + typecheck + test + smoke.

## Command trace
- `npm run verify` from the Work's worktree (HEAD = candidate e8e2b81): exitCode 0. Pipeline = typecheck + test (build + node --test dist/test/*.test.js) + smoke + node bin/codepatrol.js --help. 300/300 tests pass (16 new skill-suite tests on top of 284 from prior Works). 0 fail. Smoke passed. Help printed the expected surface including `skill test <skill-id>`. The concurrency suite from INIT-3.2 still passes (2508ms).

## Changed files
- src/core/skill-suite.ts (new, blob 2a48e12405876e5430298c6a3938d3c9b22a6047, 180 lines) — strict suite schema with three assertion kinds and five result statuses.
- src/cli/skill-evaluation.ts (new, blob d8aef824c76b36e2f72aeae4b8d4c5dc2f99e05f, 289 lines) — deterministic runner with isolated throwaway fixtures and offline-by-construction env scrubbing.
- src/cli/commands/skill.ts (modified, blob 71be93c44dd91122028a419b7e5d5fff2151750a) — skill command gains the `test <skill-id>` action.
- skills/codepatrol-verify/suite.json (new, blob 5bc0426c39157e181ebe510fed67080dcd29d881, 101 lines) — baseline protocol suite with five passing scenarios.
- src/test/skill-suite.test.ts (new, blob 2dd65ddb3d3f678f8c78df4ebfa4986efc7b8101, 195 lines, 16 tests) — parser strictness, runner statuses, isolation, identity, broken-expectation proof, shipped-suite wire.
- .codepatrol/works/INIT-1.3-add-the-deterministic-skill-evaluation-harness/work.json (canonical manifest bookkeeping).

## Residual risk
- baselineStale=true (main advanced to 880186a3 since the branch was cut) — the verification range is fixed at baseline..candidate and does not depend on the moving branch tip; the candidate itself is clean.
- Offline is by construction (env scrubbing, no remote, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0), not by sandbox. The plan names this honestly; INIT-1.5's coverage expansion may revisit it.

## No returns required
Candidate is clean, acceptance is demonstrated, evidence is complete. Verify continues to Ship.
